Commentary.Commentary: So, what do we have in store now? Sri Lanka will have to bat well, something that they are capable of. This has to be done after being on the field for close to 130 overs. Let's see what do the tourists have to offer, as Dimuth Karunaratne and Kusal Mendis walk out with the bat. Remember, the Bangladeshi bowlers could be more than a handful in known conditions.

Mahmudullah walked in when his side was 356/4. He batted well with the lower order, stitching important stands with them. The one worth 58 with Sunzamul Islam made sure that the Lankans toiled hard on the field. Unfortunately for him, he couldn't get to the coveted ton. There is nothing great to write home about the visiting bowlers, who largely looked toothless. Rangana Herath and Suranga Lakmal returned with three apiece for them.

A very good score for the hosts, something that should have the tourists worried. Bangladesh have done just what they had set out to do after winning the toss yesterday. Their top four scored above 40s and that laid them the platform. Aided by a monumental stand between Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim, that was worth 236 runs, the hosts tired out the opposing bowlers. Haque stroked his way to a well-compiled 176 and would be ruing missing out on his double ton. Rahim should also be cursing himself to have thrown it away at the fag end on Day 1.

Nice shot? Oh no! BANGLADESH ALL OUT! This is banged short again on the stumps, Rahman initially looks to duck. As an afterthought, he decides to play the ramp over the keeper and that's that. Doesn't make the contact as he would have liked and ends up hitting it in the air to offer an easy catch to Dickwella. So, to add to the list of Rahim and Haque, who missed out getting to their milestones, add Mahmudullah, who is left stranded 17 runs short of the triple figure mark. The hosts finish on 513.
WIDE! Bouncer on off, Rahman ducks and lets it go. Wide given for height.
Full and tailing in around off and middle, driven down to long off for one.
Outside off, glided down to third man for nothing.
Banged short in line of the stumps, he gets out of the way to let it be.

How long should Bangladesh bat? Athar Ali Khan says that there is no dearth of time and hence they should bat on. Opines that their skipper should target his ton, which is just 18 runs away at the moment.
Fuller in length, Mahmudullah paddles it down to fine leg for a brace.
Very full outside off, Rahman misses jamming that out.
Flatter on off, defended from the crease.
SIX! Even I can bat skip, says Rahman! Sees the tossed up ball in his zone, clears the front leg and goes over long on for a maximum. The stand is worth 31 now.
On off, defended from the crease.
Driven through covers for one. Now Fizz has to see off the last 4 balls of the over.
Floated full on middle and leg, Mahmudullah gets down and paddles it fine down the leg side for a couple.
Fuller on off from round the wicket, pushed back towards the bowler.
The chest guard comes out for Mustafizur Rahman. With the number of batters taking blows to their body, it is good to get yourself guarded.
Short in length, pulled through square leg. This time the skipper ambles to the other end and moves to 77. 500 runs up for the hosts.
Bumper in line of the stumps, Mahmudullah arches back and lets it be. It goes on the bounce to the keeper.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Back of a length ball outside off, guided to third man for nothing.
On a length outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Suranga Lakmal is back into the attack.
Huge cheers go around as Rahman sees off the last ball of the over with a block towards covers. A maiden for Herath.
Another one outside off, defended towards point.
Arm ball outside off, The Fizz prods forward to defend but gets beaten on the outside.
Just outside off, defended back towards the bowler.
Landed around off, defended off the front foot.
Floated around off, driven back to the bowler.
Punched off the back foot by Mahmudullah.
Around middle and leg, pushed to mid on.
Similar delivery, similar shot, no run.
Outside off, pushed through covers for nothing.

SIX! Ho, ho, ho, it's a beauty! Shows that he picked up the conventional spin early. Floated full on the stumps, Mahmudullah gets his front leg out of the way and smashes it high over the bowler's head for half a dozen. Bangladesh are one short of 500, while the skipper is on 76.
FOUR! Rubbish ball! Flatter and shorter outside off, perhaps an attempted googly. Mahmudullah goes deep back and slaps it through cover-point for a boundary. That's 2000 Test runs for him.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Mistimed back towards the bowler.
Eased down to long on to rotate strike.

More confusion! Rahman punches this one off the back foot towards covers. The fielder dives to his left and parries it to his left. He tries to recover himself to prevent a run but fails to do so. After some yes and no, the run is completed, even as a wild shy is had at the bowler's end.

Confusion, no harm done! Rahman taps this one towards covers and stays where he is. His skipper is down half the way before he denies the single. Mahmudullah has to rush back hurriedly and does so beating the fielder's throw to his end.
Fuller on off, driven back to the bowler.
FOUR! Bang! Floated full on the stumps, Mahmudullah gets his front leg out of the way and hits it over mid-wicket for a boundary.

WIDE BUT A STUMPING CHANCE MISSED! Oh, Dickwella, you need to have a calm head, mate! Fired flatter and wider outside off, seeing Mahmudullah charge down. He tried to reach to it but missed. Niroshan, in an attempt to inflict the stumping, fails to gather the ball and that allows the batter to get in safely. The keeper had stumped the batter in his mind much before reality, hence he ended up letting the chance go.
Hit through covers, a single denied.
Flatter and quicker on the stumps, Mahmudullah goes back to flick it but gets an inside edge onto the pads. Missing leg, says Roshen Abeysinghe on air, but no sir, he has hit that.
Flicked away off the pads for nothing.
Full on off, driven down to long off for nothing.
Flatter outside off, Mahmudullah goes back and guides it through backward point for none.
Full in length at 75 kph, Rahman gets his bat down in time to keep it to the off side.
Floated around middle and off, hit inside out to long off for one.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated around leg, Mahmudullah defends it off the front foot.
Similar delivery on a similar line, Mahmudullah fails to defend it and wears it on the pads.
Arm delivery on the pads, Mahmudullah misses hitting that.
Fuller in length, eased down to long on for one.
Deep backward square leg also comes in.
Lovely delivery. Floated up in line of the stumps, Mahmudullah makes room to go through the off side but just manages to get an inside edge onto his pads.
Now the field comes in to prevent the single.
Yorker on the stumps, dug out to the bowler.
Around off, defended back towards the bowler.
Sri Lanka are offering easy singles to the opposing skipper so that they can have a go at the last man. The long off fielder is in place and this ball is hit to him. But the run is not taken.
Googly well outside off, Mahmudullah covers the stumps and lets it go.
Kept out towards mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Arm ball around off, driven through covers for one.
Outside off, edged past slip for a run to get going.
Mustafizur Rahman is the last man in.

OUT! Dream delivery to any batsman leave alone the tailender. Tossed up outside off, Islam lunges forward to block but leaves some gap between bat and pad. The ball lands in the rough there and spins in sharply to peg back the LEG STUMP. Alarming turn, elates the Lankans this time. They are one wicket away from ending their time on the field.
Around off, defended off the front foot.
Punched through point for a brace. Mahmudullah moves to 58.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Around middle and leg, turned past short leg for one.
Taijul Islam strides out to bat at no.10 for Bangladesh.

STUMPED OUT! Yes, Islam is well down the track but the margin of dismissal is not as much as we thought it to be. Sandakan spots Sunzamul being ready to charge down the track and fires this down the leg side. The number 9 misses the flick post that and Dickwella uproots the stumps and goes up in celebration. On the first look he seems to be a clear goner but the third umpire is called for. Replays show that he is just short of the crease as the keeper had to collect it well to his right and then go for the stumping. Sri Lanka finally manage to get through this stubborn stand.
Islam should be a goner! The TV umpire is referred to for a stumping appeal against Sunzamul. Seems to be well down the track on the first look...
Outside off, slapped through cover-point for one.
Around off, defended with a lunge forward.
Lakshan Sandakan to bowl from the other end. A slip and FSL in place.
Outside off, edged towards point.
Forward defense displayed to this one on the stumps.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Glorious. Tossed up outside off, Mahmudullah slinks down the track in no time and drives it through covers. It is played all along the ground and the ball races away to the fence.
Outside off, Islam guides it towards third man to rotate strike.

The skipper is leading from the front. 15th Test fifty for Mahmudullah. Gets a full length tossed up ball around off, driven towards covers. De Silva dives but fails to stop it and ends up parrying it towards long off. One run taken and the home skipper raises his bat to acknowledge the applause.

Welcome back. The men who matter have taken their positions on the field. Sri Lanka have some more time to spend on the field before they can get into the batting mode. For now, Mahmudullah will face Rangana Herath first up.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

The tourists looked like running through Bangladesh's lower order, when they struck quickly, courtesy the wily old fox Rangana Herath, who picked up a couple of wickets to get his name in the wickets' column. He is constantly getting something out of the track, that is slowing down considerably. What should worry them, however, is that none of the others have looked threatening for a considerable time. With the position that the hosts find themselves in, we can expect some quick runs in the post-lunch session. Do join us then to see if Sri Lanka have it in them to see the end of this innings quickly.

Comeback and fightback - the tale of the morning. Sri Lanka started the day on a positive note by landing crucial blows quickly. At the end of the first hour, they were successful in picking up three wickets, conceding just 43 in 12.2 overs. But post that, the script came back to normal, as the hosts continued to amass more runs. Mahmudullah and Sunzamul Islam have added 50 for the 8th wicket and are looking too good to be dislodged. Mominul Haque, sadly for them, couldn't add much to his overnight score and was the first one to depart this morning.
Floated on the stumps, Islam lunges forward and defends it watchfully to go into LUNCH, DAY 2, unbeaten.
Outside off, driven to the man at mid off.
Islam gets behind that solidly and defends it.
Punched off the back foot by Sunzamul.

Flatter on the pads, worked away to fine leg for a run. That's the 50-run partnership between Mahmudullah and Islam. They were staring at a collapse when the debutant walked in and have done well to keep the tourists at bay since then.
Floated around leg, flicked away towards mid-wicket.
This should be the last over before lunch. Dhananjaya de Silva to roll his arm over.
Mahmudullah pushes it towards covers and quickly gets to the other end. The stand moves to 49 now.
Another lovely delivery. Tossed up on middle and leg, Mahmudullah looks to defend with a prod. The ball turns away yet again and passes just close to the outside edge and the off pole.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Turn! Floated up around off, Mahmudullah lunges forward to defend but the ball spins away sharply to beat him.
This ball is defended towards point from the crease.
Fuller in line of the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Rangana Herath back on for another spell.
Flatter on off, Mahmudullah moves to 47 by guiding it to deep backward point for one.
Fuller in length, defended back towards the bowler.
Tossed up around off, swept away to deep mid-wicket for one.
This is outside off, pushed towards point.
Floated full around off, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Flighted in line of the stumps, Islam goes back and pushes it towards covers.
Straight in line of the stumps, played to short leg.
Served around middle and leg, Islam gets it off the inner half past short leg for one.
Flatter outside off, Mahmudullah goes back and cuts it just past slip. Gets three runs for the same. He moves to 46 and this stand is worth 45 now.
Knocked down to long off for a single.

Floated outside off, Islam gets down the track to defend but seems to have got an inside edge onto the pads and the ball rolls to the off side. Dickwella yells in appeal but our scorer shouts that the batter has hit it. Nope! It is all pad, shows the replay.
Floated full around off, defended with a lunge forward.
Bowled well outside off, Mahmudullah has nothing to do with it.
On the stumps, swept to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Floated outside off, Islam has a lazy poke at it off the front foot but misses as the ball spins away.
Flatter outside off, cut away for one.
This ball is knocked through mid-wicket for one.
Well outside off, chopped towards point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. 8 runs off the over.
Mahmudullah defends this one off the front foot.
The batsman has edged that one. They pick up a single.
Mahmudullah rotates strike by hitting this through mid on.
Flatter down the leg side, left alone.
SIX! Bang! It's time for Mahmudullah to free his arms now. Gets a tossed up ball around middle and leg, he comes down the track and hits it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.

NOT OUT! Excellent umpiring from Rod Tucker. Sandakan tosses up a wrong 'un around off, Islam lunges forward to play for the conventional spin. Misses and gets rapped on the front pad and the ball goes to the slip fielder. The Lankans appeal to no avail. Chandimal immediately opts for the DRS. The TV umpire asks the on-field umpire whether it is referred for a catch or LBW. Gets confirmation that it is for the former. The Snicko is used to see that there is no inside edge. In fact, there is a huge daylight between bat and the ball. Now, the LBW is checked and the Ball Tracker shows that it would have gone down leg. So the on-field call stays and Sri Lanka lose a review. Mr. Tucker has been good on the field so far. Yesterday he spotted that the visitors had more-than-permissible number of players behind square on the leg side and ruled it a no ball and now this one. Well done, sir!
Sri Lanka feel they have got their man. An appeal is made but the umpire negates the same. Chandimal signals a 'T'. What is the review for? An appeal for catch against Islam.
WIDE! Very, very wide outside off, Islam lets it be. The umpire has to stretch his arms.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
FOUR! Thumped! Floated outside off, Islam takes a couple of steps down the track and blasts it straight over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Gone, almost! Floated outside off, Islam looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge. It lands just short of Karunaratne at first slip.
Shortish in length outside off, Mahmudullah slaps it through covers and gets to the other end.
Wrong 'un outside off, Mahmudullah stays back and bunts it.
Bowled in line of the stumps, stonewalled from the crease.
Outside off and spinning further away, Islam looks to play it through covers but misses. The bails are whipped off in a flash but he is well in.
Around off, SI slinks down and defends it.
Floated on the stumps, defended with a lunge forward.
Flatter ball, goes on with the arm. Islam fails to flick it away and wears it on the pads.

Begins with a delivery outside off, Mahmudullah goes back and guides it to third man for one. He is happy to not hound the strike and rotate it even with the presence of a lower order batter at the other end.
Dilruwan Perera to have a bowl now. He is two short of 100 runs!
Islam gets down the track and bunts it down.
Served in line of the stumps, mistimed to mid on.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Flatter googly outside off, Islam tries to cut but fails.

Almost strikes! Flatter in trajectory, it is the quicker one. Sunzamul goes back to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads and the ball lands just behind the stumps on the off side. Dickwella is aware of the bat component in that and goes for the catch but is out of reach. Sandakan meanwhile puts in a stifled appeal for LBW which isn't entertained.
Floated full outside off, Islam gets his stride out and drives it nicely through covers. Before the mopping up is done in the deep, a couple results.
Around off, pushed through cover-point to retain strike.
Punched to the man at sweeper to rotate strike.
Tossed up delivery on the stumps, driven straight to mid on. Chandimal there ends up parrying it behind the bowler and a run is taken.

Herath is getting into the groove here with some assistance from the surface. Tosses this one outside off, Islam lunges forward to defend. The ball spins in, but not as much as Sunzamul expected. Ends up getting beaten on the outside edge.
Outside off, pushed through covers for one.
Floated on the stumps, defended off the front foot.
Flipped around off, Islam hurriedly punches it towards covers.
Flatter on the stumps, kept out from the crease.

Lovely ball. Sandakan bowls a googly around off, it goes away after pitching. Squares up Mahmudullah a touch, who somehow manages to keep it out towards backward point. His partner calls him for a run and he responds later. The slowness of the surface helped the batter here. On a quicker track, he could have edged it to the fielder.
Defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Outside off, driven towards mid off.
Flatter outside off, Mahmudullah hangs back and keeps it out with a straight bat.
Lakshan Sandakan for the first time today. Can he hasten the end for Bangladesh? A slip and a short leg in place.
Around off, driven to mid off.
Worked round the corner for a single.
Mahmudullah strides forward to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Mahmudullah lunges forward and blocks it.
Floated up on off, eased through mid on for one.
Played to the point region by Islam. They pick up a single.
This ball is played through point for one.
Length ball outside off, Sunzamul punches it through covers. Three runs are taken as Herath chases it down and saves a run for his side. Good effort from the veteran.

Nice point. The pitch has showed its treacherous side today. Earlier in the pitch report this morning, Tino Mawoyo cited variable bounce that could be a factor and that's what we saw on more than one occasions so far. Lakmal bowled a short delivery that failed to climb up and almost slid through on its way to the keeper. Another one from a similar spot rose to such an extent that the batter had to keep it out awkwardly even with a hop. Wonder if this would excite the Lankans or worry them, as they would be batting at some point today.
Outside off, pushed through covers for one.
Good running. Islam taps this back of a length ball towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Banged short on the stumps, Islam gets away from the line and lets it be.
Herath comes round the wicket to Mahmudullah and delivers it on the stumps. Blocked off the front foot.
Eased through mid on for a single.
Outside off, driven to mid off.

Floated outside off, the ball turns in after pitching. Islam goes back to defend but misses and gets struck on the pads. An appeal followed but it is turned down. Sliding down leg, as confirmed by Hawk Eye.
Islam gets foward and pushes it through point for a brace.
On off, defended off the back foot.
Mahmudullah sees this off with a forward defense.
Short in length, Mahmudullah stands tall and blocks it to the leg side.
FOUR! Well played. On a length outside off, Mahmudullah stands tall and flays it past gully for a boundary.
Mahmudullah has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This is bowled in line of the stumps, defended from the crease.
On a length in the line of the stumps, blocked with an angled bat to the off side.
Beaten again! Drifting in from around off and then straightens a bit. Debutant lunges forward to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge of his bat.
Driven towards the fielder at mid off.
Beaten! Looks to play for the turn but there isn't any.
Floated delivery outside off, Islam looks to defend but gets an inside edge towards short leg.
Sunzamul Islam strides in next.
The wicket of Mehidy Hasan has led to the drinks break.

OUT! Run Out! Even the dive doesn't save Mehidy Hasan. Flatter delivery outside off, Mahmudullah dabs it past the lone slip fielder and sets off. Karunarante from slip gives it a chase and so does Kumara who sprints across to his left from third man. Mehidy calls for the third run to which his skipper responds. The pacer gets to the ball and returns a throw to Dickwella who collects and takes the bails off as the batsman dives to get back in. Looked really close and they take it upstairs. Replays show that the bails had come off and then the bat came in. Enough for the TV umpire to rule it out. Bangladesh are throwing it away.
Yes, no and eventually they go for it. There is a run out appeal which is referred upstairs. Mehidy Hasan is the man in question and looks to be a goner...
Very full and fired on off, jammed out towards the cover fielder.
Very full and sprayed wider outside off, the batsman crouches low and squeezes it out behind point and shall keep strike.
Digs in a short ball, something he did more often yesterday. Mahmudullah ducks under it.
Angles it in from outside off, Mahmudullah stays back in defense.
Hasan spanks this one through cover but will get just a single.
Fuller in length on the stumps, punched down past the man at mid on for a brace.
Starts off with a shortish ball from over the wicket, safely kept out off the back foot.
Lahiru Kumara is the first bowling change of the morning.
Quick single! On middle and leg, Mehidy pushes it towards Sandakan at mid on and calls through for a brisk run.
Takes a stride forward and drives it towards the cover fielder.

SIX! Slogged away! What a hit and he admires it himself! Herath generously tosses it up on the stumps, Hasan sits down on one knee and slogs it high and mighty over the deep mid-wicket fence for a maximum.
More loopy, around off, blocked.
Flatter outside off, punched off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery, wider on off, Hasan presses forward to drive but gets a thick inside edge past the leg stump. The ball rolls towards the man at 45.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Goes back and clips it through square leg for a single.

FOUR! Shot of the morning! Fuller in length, it's delivered on off, Mehidy Hasan prods ahead and drives it straight back down the ground. First it beats the bowler who tries to stop it with his right boot in the followthrough and then it beats the dive of Kumara at mid off. Races away to the fence to bring up the 400 for Bangladesh!
Lakma pitches it right up there, Mehidy leans forward and drives it through covers for a another couple.
Another one on the same length, Hasan covers the line and punches it down the ground through mid on. Takes a brace.
Shortish outside off, punched off the back foot to the cover fielder.

Good delivery! A slider, at 89.1 kph, it's on the shorter length and goes through with the arm. Mahmudullah sits back to play the late cut but the ball nearly takes the outside edge and settles into the gloves of Dickwella.
Loops it up outside off, the skipper comes down the track and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Stays leg side and drives it square on the off side. The man from backward point gives it a chase but they run two.
Slower through the air, pitches on middle and turns away towards off, Mahmudullah lunges forward to defend but gets an inside edge towards short leg.
Comes down the track and keeps it out watchfully.
Floated ball outside off, blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Mehidy lunges forward to keep it out back to the bowler.
Taps it in front of point and scampers through for a quick single.
Angles it in from outside off, a compact defense on offer.
Shortish and rising a bit off the surface, Mahmudullah takes his bottom hand off and defends it in front of the point fielder.
Fuller and angling in on the stumps, defended back to the bowler.
Short of a length ball, very close to the off stump line, Mahmudullah makes room to dab it on the bounce to the gully fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted delivery on middle and off, Hasan defends it off the inner half to FSL.
Tossed up ball outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
A bit short, turns away ever so slightly, Mahmudullah dabs it behind point to collect one.
Loopy delivery outside off, pushed towards cover for a single.
Mehidy Hasan walks in next.

OUT! Straight to mid on! Poor shot to be honest! Herath spots that Hossain is giving him the charge and hence he tosses it on leg, following the batsman. The ball pitches and turns in just a bit. The batsman is already down the track and hence goes on with the lofted shot. Spoons it off the inner half and hands a simple catch to Lakshan Sandakan at mid on, who pouches it with a couple of steps backwards. So, Bangladesh lose their second wicket for just 16 runs in 37 balls this morning. Collapse on the cards?
Stays back and pushes it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Risky leave! Lands it on a length outside off, it threatens to come back in. Mahmudullah plants his front foot across and then makes a leave.

FOUR! Just wide of the gully fielder! Suranga with another short ball and this time he offers width. The Bangla skipper goes chasing after it with a wild slash. Gets a thick edge which travels towards gully where Dilruwan Perera dives to his right but couldn't get to it. Streaky boundary results!

The track is playing its tricks now! This one kicks off the deck, Mosaddek rises on the toes to hit it away but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls away towards the off side. They take a single.

What was that? That didn't rise at all. Smiles on the faces of the Lankan players. Lakmal bangs in a short one, outside off, Hossain looks to pull but the ball sits really low and sneaks through to the keeper. Luckily for the batsman, this delivery wasn't on the stumps.
Darted around the pads, clipped wide of mid on to keep strike.
Tossed up delivery on the stumps, blocked watchfully.
This time he pushes it through the air, Mosaddek pushes at it awkwardly.

Almost a wicket! Some turn on offer for Herath. Beautifully bowled! Slower through the air, a bit short and then it grips off the surface. Opens up Hossain completely who goes back and doesn't know what to do. Dangles his bat at it and is lucky that the edge didn't carry to the first slip fielder.
Gets forward and defends it into the ground.
Goes wide of the crease and with a round-arm action he slides it outside off, Mahmudullah takes a stride forward and pushes it through cover for a single.
Stays back and defends  it back to Lakmal.
Marginally short, in the corridor outside off, MH shows a straight blade.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, the batsman hops to keep it out.
FOUR! On the up! A bit too full and a bit too wide, Hossain decides to cash in on it. He leans forward and drives it square of the wicket on the off side to pick up his first boundary.
Kicks off the deck from the shorter length, Mosaddek hops back and fends it towards square leg.
Inside edge! Lakmal keeps it on a length, serves it outside off, Mahmudullah tries to push this one away but ekes out an inside edge which rolls behind square on the leg side for a single.
Loopy ball, a bit wider outside off, Hossain makes room and drives it through the gap at cover to get off the mark with a couple of runs. Successful over from the veteran.
Tosses it up on the stumps, Hossain presses forward in defense but does so off the inner half of the bat.
Mosaddek Hossain is the new man in.

OUT! Chipped straight to short leg! Excellent take from Kusal Mendis!  Rangana Herath strikes for the first time in the game. Not a good ball but Sri Lanka wouldn't mind it at all. From over the wicket, Rangana tosses it up around middle and leg, Haque comes down the track and looks to flick it away. He does so but it goes straight towards short leg where it hits Mendis on the left side of the chest. The fielder is aware and does well to grab it in the second attempt. Soft dismissal to say the least. So, no ton for Rahim, no double ton for Haque either as he adds just a run to his overnight tally. Half the side back in the hut for the hosts.
Flighted ball outside off, pushed with an open bat face to backward point.
Loops it up around off, pushed towards cover for a single.
Flighted ball around middle and off, Mahmudullah buries it into the ground.
Back of a length delivery, outside off, defended nicely off the back foot. A maiden for Lakmal.
Good line! Tempting delivery from outside off, Mominul shoulders his arms to that one.
Switches the angle, comes from around the wicket, Mominul tries to dab it away but fails to get any wood on it.
On a length and around middle and off, MH covers the line and defends.
Slightly short and hurled outside off, Mominul stands tall and cuts it nicely but finds the man at cover-point who dives to his right to make a stop.
Good length delivery, angling away around the fifth stump channel, Haque watches it go through to the keeper.
Suranga Lakmal will bowl from the other end. When the things were looking rather dismal for Sri Lanka, he came back well to make inroads at the fag end of day 1. Can he strike early today?
Tossed up delivery around middle and off, Mahmudullah steps out of the crease to block but wears it on the pads. Tidy stuff to kick things off.
Presses forward and kills it back down on the surface.
Flighted ball around middle and off, the batsman comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Comes down the track does Mominul and eases it towards long on for a single. First run of the day.
Slightly slower, at 81.7 kph, Haque keeps it out off the front foot.
Floats it up from over the wicket, Haque prods forward and flicks it a bit uppishly towards the man at short mid-wicket.
We are set to get rolling. The players and umpires have made their way out to the middle. Mominul Haque will face Rangana Herath. A slip and a short leg in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo says it's still a batting paradise and the conditions haven't changed a lot. Adds there was some variable bounce on offer from the good length area yesterday and feels as the game progresses, the pacers will have their say.

Day 1 was all about the batters dictating terms. Everyone came in and had fun apart from Liton Das. The hosts are well on course to post a huge first innings total and they have Mominul Haque who is leading the way with an unbeaten 175. Sri Lanka would be looking to come out afresh and make the second new ball, which is just 60 balls old, count. Can Sri Lanka enforce a collapse from hereon? Hello and welcome to our coverage of the second day's play. Stay with us as the action isn't that far away...
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Right then! Quick wickets shall be the key for the visitors and if they manage to do so early in the morning tomorrow, they will still feel they are in the game. Will they be able to restrict the hosts or will Bangladesh continue to march on? We shall find out tomorrow on day 2. Join us at 0930 Local (0330 GMT) to catch all the action. Until then, goodbye and cheers!

The Sri Lankans, after being made to toil hard, needed someone to lift them up again. The second new ball did the trick for them late in the day. It was Suranga Lakmal who struck twice in successive balls and importantly he broke the massive 236-run stand. Liton Das bagged a golden duck but Haque and Mahmudullah then did well to see off the remainder of the day. All the bowlers had a tough day at the office. Dilruwan Perera and Lakshan Sandakan got the first two wickets but then failed to make any impact. Lahiru Kumara was very inconsistent and went for aplenty. The wily spinner, too, didn't look penetrative enough and as a result they let Bangladesh dominate the day.

Mominul Haque walked out with other ideas. He stepped on the gas and accelerated as soon as he got into the groove to keep the visitors' bowlers at bay. Mushfiqur Rahim gave him perfect company as the pair toyed with and ripped the bowling apart. The pitch hardly had anything in it but it still required some batting to get runs. Both of them motored along at a healthy run rate and broke a few records in the process.

That ends the proceedings on the opening day of the Test. Bangladesh are the ones who take the honours as they make the most of winning the toss and electing to bat by posting a big total on the board. Mind you, they aren't done yet. It all started with Tamim Iqbal in the morning who came out with a lot intent. He blazed a quick fifty to give his team an ideal start. Imrul Kayes played well for his 40 but both the openers were sent back in the first session and it seemed like Sri Lanka have got the opening.
Fuller in length and drifting a bit on the pads, Mahmudullah shuffles a touch and clips it towards the man at backward square leg. STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Another short one, kicks off the deck, Mahmudullah arches back to evade it.
Ahead of a length and angling in, bunted towards the cover fielder.
Bangs in a short one outside off, bends his back on this one. The Bangla skipper is quick to sway away from the line.
Angling in from over the wicket to the right-hander, it's kept out back to the bowler.
Shorter in length and angling in from around the wicket, Haque opens the face of the bat to glide it towards point for a single.
So, last over of the day is coming up. Will Sri Lanka send half the Bangladesh side back in the hut? Here comes Lakmal...
Herath gives it nice loop and keeps it full on off, Mahmudullah leans ahead and strokes it to the man at cover.
Bends forward to defend this one but gets it off the inner half towards short leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Shimmies down the track and eases it down to long on for a single.
Flighted ball around off, driven towards mid off for a single.
Loopy delivery, slower through the air, lands outside off. Mominul comes forward to push it away but gets it off the outer edge past the gully fielder for a couple.

Switches the angle again for the last ball of the over. From over the wicket, he keeps it on a fuller length outside off. Haque pushes it towards mid off and calls for the single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Goes around the wicket and angles in a length delivery on middle, tucked into the leg side.
Digs in a short one, but on the leg stump, easily ducked under.
Goes fuller, it's on the stumps, defended back to Lakmal.

Haque almost edges this! Lovely piece of bowling from the Lankan vice-captain! He slants it away in the tempting line outside off, Haque looks to play at it but the ball leaves the southpaw and whizzes past the outside edge of his bat.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Slower through the air, around middle and off. Mahmudullah punches it towards mid on where Kumara makes a meal of it. Lets it through and then gives it a long chase. He slides and pulls the ball back in play at long on. The umpire checks it upstairs and after watching a lot of replays, the TV umpire feels that the Lankan pacer made simultaneous contact with the rope and the ball.
FOUR! Good looking shot! Flighted ball around middle and off, Mahmudullah comes down the track and lofts it over mid on to get off the mark in style.

Almost... almost another! Herath has his hands on his head in disbelief! He bowls a slider, Mahmudullah didn't read it at all. It keeps coming in with the angle and the Bangla skipper is lucky to get his bat down in time. Gets an inside edge as the ball rolls towards square leg.
Around the leg stump, Mahmudullah defends.
Tossed up on off, Mominul drives it towards point where Roshen makes a half-stop and concedes a single.
The batsman stands behind the line to keep it out.
Very full, almost a yorker, the batsman does well to keep that at bay.
Back of a length outside off, punched off the back foot towards point.
That's a risky leave! On a length, pitched outside off as Mahmudullah shoulders his arms. This one didn't nip back in the way it did to dismiss Das. But even this wasn't far from the off pole.
Ahead of a length outside off, Mahmudullah drives it towards Roshen Silva at point who makes a good stop.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Back of a length delivery outside off, steered square of the wicket on the off side for a single. No hat-trick for Lakmal.
Takes a stride forward and dives it to the cover fielder.
Mahmudullah lunges forward to defend but misses to get hit on the pads.
Loops it up on off, watchfully kept out.
Punched off the back foot through cover for a single.
Floated delivery around off, blocked down.
Flatter through the air, defended off the back foot.
Mahmudullah, the Bangladesh skipper walks in next. No nightwatchman? Interesting.

OUT! Off stump goes for a walk! One brings two as the saying goes! An error in judgement from Das means that Lakmal now will be on a hat-trick in the next over. Sri Lanka rejoice! Lakmal hurls a length ball outside off, Liton Das leans forward and thinks that he has his off stump covered but the ball nips back in to take it apart. Das walks back for a golden duck, which happens to be the first blob in his Test career. Can Sri Lanka pick up another?
Liton Das walks out to bat next.

OUT! Lakmal induces an edge! Finally, finally Sri Lanka taste success after the first session today. Suranga keeps it on a length and in the avenue of apprehension. Rahim with no feet movement goes after this one. The ball bounces just a bit more, takes the outer half of the bat and settles into the mitts of Dickwella behind. The second new ball has done the trick for Sri Lanka. Rahim stands there in dismay as he misses out on a deserving ton. This is the third time in Tests that Rahim has been dismissed in the nervous nineties. Seemed like it was a lapse in concentration from the wicket-keeper batsman. Nonetheless, the 236-run stand has been broken.
On a length and around middle and off, MR stands back in defense.
Steers it behind point and scampers through for a single.
Fuller in length outside off, driven through covers for a single.
Shortish and on the fourth stump line, tapped in front of point for a single.
No ball! Fuller in length and angling in on middle, flicked straight to the man at short mid-wicket. Lakmal oversteps and so he will have to reload.
FOUR! Into the 90s goes Rahim! Herath bowls a poor delivery, short and outside off, Mushfiqur slaps it through point to end the over with a boundary.
Floated delivery outside off, blocked into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted delivery outside off, defended down watchfully.
Punched down to long off for a single.

Haque is getting some massage on his back. Understandably. He has been out there for quite a while now and gets a bit of treatment from the physio. Meanwhile, the umpire is seen trimming the thread on the seam.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The floodlights have been turned on.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Easily done! Fuller in length and sprays it on the pads, Rahim gets across and clips it neatly through mid-wicket and picks up a boundary. The runs keep coming with the new ball as well, 16 runs off 10 balls.
Ahead of a length and on the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller in length and angling in, worked towards mid on.
Good length delivery outside off, Rahim stands tall and with an open bat face he guides it behind point and runs brace.
Suranga Lakmal to share the new cherry with Herath.
Punched off the back foot by MH.

SIX! Takes on the veteran! Mominul Haque now has another milestone. He becomes the quickest to 2K Test runs for Bangladesh, in just 47 innings. Floated ball outside off, Haque dances down the track, isn't quite to the pitch of the ball but still looks to go big. Slices it but still has enough the clear the long off fence for a maximum.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets behind the line and blocks it out.

FOUR! Edged and through! Slower through the air, lands full outside off, Mominul Haque presses forward to push it away but the ball takes the outside edge and flies past the lone slip fielder who despite a dive can't get to it. A boundary in a streaky manner.
Starts off from over the wicket and bowls a flatter one on middle and off, Mominul punches it back to the bowler.

Second new ball is available now and the Lankans have taken it straightaway. It will be Rangana Herath to taste the new cherry first. Can the new ball bring about a change in fortunes for them? Final 10 overs of the day coming up...
Shortish and angling away, Haque cuts it to deep point for a single.
Fuller and wider on off, driven on the up but finds mid off.

Pitches it up outside off, driven on the up but straight to mid off.

Back of a length delivery on middle and off, punched off the back foot towards cover.

Hangs back and defends it down gently.

BUMP BALL! Not out! Sandakan bowls it full around the pads, Rahim works it towards the man at short leg who collects and immediately releases the ball at the bowler's end. Is it a bump ball? Seems so but the umpire doesn't want to take any chance and refers it upstairs. Mushfiqur Rahim is the man in question...

How easily Haque gets to his 150! This is the second time he has reached this milestone. Slower leg break, worked against the turn through mid-wicket for an easy single. Raises the bat as the whole Bangladesh dressing room stands up to applaud the effort.
A bat-pad in place now as Haque is one short of 150.

Tucked through the square leg region for a single.

FOUR! That's flayed! Brings up the double century stand between these two! The runs keep coming for the hosts and they continue to rule the roost. Short ball, wider outside off, Rahim rises on his toes, gets properly on top of the bounce and slaps it through point for a boundary to beat the dive of the fielder.

On middle and leg, worked down to long on for a single.

The throw came towards the first slip fielder, who collects and hits the stumps at the bowler's end. The ball deflects further but they don't run another.

Dances down the track and wrists it towards mid-wicket for nothing.
Slider around middle and off, Mushfiq presses forward in defense.

Stopped a certain boundary, de Silva! Fuller in length on middle and off, Mominul brings his bat down at the angle and drives it back down the ground. Shortish delivery on middle and leg, pulled with control through backward square leg for a brace.
Good length ball, in the channel outside off, left alone.

Flighted ball around off, defended down watchfully.
Comes from around the wicket and drifts in on middle and off, blocked off the front foot.
Fuller on the stumps, bunted back down the track. Herath, in his followthrough tries to stop it with his left boot but fails. A single picked up as the ball rolls down to long on.
Slower through the air, wider on off, Haque has all the time in the world to go back and dab it away down to third man. He gets two for doing so.
Tossed up on middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Floats it up around middle, it skids off, Mominul goes back and defends it towards short mid-wicket.

Drinks time! Runs. That sums it all. Haque and Rahim have ensured that the visiting side doesn't have it easy. Their partnership is worth 182 now. Rahim lunges forward and blocks it off the front foot.
On the pads, turned through square leg for one.

Flatter in trajectory in line of the stumps, Mominul goes back and flicks it through mid-wicket. They take one but seeing the fielder being slow to get to the ball, they think about the second. But the man in the deep does well to keep it down to one less than two.
Around off and middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Flatter on the stumps, Rahim gets down and paddles it to fine leg for one.
Outside off, driven through covers to rotate strike.
Aimed in line of the stumps, MH goes back and defends.
Eased down to long on for a single.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Flatter on the stumps, Rahim lunges forward to defend but gets it off the inner half towards fine leg for one.
Outside off, pushed towards point.

Tossed up around middle and leg, Rahim shimmies down the ground and hits it over mid-wicket. There is protection in the deep and hence just one run is the outcome.

Driven nicely through mid off for one.
Flighted generously, Rahim whips it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, pushed towards covers.

Rangana Herath is brought back. He has just bowled 9 overs today and has been wicketless so far. Can he provide his side the breakthrough that they desperately need?

FOUR! Nicely struck. Floated full outside off, Rahim gets down and plays the slog sweep to perfection. Gets a boundary through deep mid-wicket.
In line of the stumps, wristed to mid-wicket.
Haque goes back to this one and whips it away for a single through mid-wicket.
Eased through covers for one.
Driven through mid on by the batsman.
Short in length, pulled away towards short fine leg. A misfield there allows him a couple. 150-run partnership between these two.
Rahim pushes it towards coves and gets to the other end.

Perera spots Haque charging and bowls it a touch short. He has to defend it to the off side.

DROPPED? Seems so, as the umpire has given this as a run off the bat. Short ball down the leg side, Haque goes for the pull but seems to have got a tickle. The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Short in length outside off, slapped away through covers to bring up RAHIM'S 19TH TEST FIFTY. He has held fort on one end as Haque has been attacking from the other.

This ball is driven through covers to rotate strike. The stand moves to 142.
Around off, Mominul drives it back. Perera dives to his right and makes a half-stop. Nothing conceded though.
Floated around off, defended towards covers for none.
Flat outside off, cut away to backward point.
Bowled full down the leg side, swept straight to short fine leg. Rahim stays on 48.
Full outside off, driven to sweeper for one.
Flattish outside off, slapped through covers for one.
Outside off, hit to point.
Mushfiqur lunges forward and defends it to short leg.

On the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket.
On off, kept out towards mid off.

Served on the stumps, Haque dances down and defends.
Fuller on off, driven straight back.
Well outside off, left alone.

Floated full outside off, Rahim hits it straight back to where it came from.
Outside off, punched through covers for one.

Flatter on off, MH goes back and keeps it out.
Lakshan Sandakan to continue his spell. A slip and a FSL in place.
Eased through mid on to retain strike.
Fuller on the stumps, pushed towards mid on.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Around off, pushed towards mid off.
Full outside off, driven to covers. Perera has overstepped and hence it is a no ball.

Welcome back! 34 overs left in the day. If spinners bowl the majority of them, which I think they should, we should get most of them in time. But stranger things have happened in the sport. Out walk the men who matter. Mominul Haque will face Dilruwan Perera to begin the proceedings.

It is imperative to know the right pace to bowl on a track and Sri Lanka have erred just there. Their spinners have been guilty of being a touch too short on a slow-paced track and have paid the price. In the first session, at least their pacers looked like picking up a wicket. In this one, no one seemed threatening. To say that all their bowlers looked flat, is an understatement. Will the final session see a change in the narrative? We'll be glad to have you with us shortly, as it gets unveiled.

Bangladesh's session without an ounce of doubt. They continued to run riot with the bat, a run rate of close to 4.50 an over shows just that. Mominul Haque brought up an attacking ton, his 5th in Tests, while Mushfiqur Rahim is three shy of his fifty. They are amidst an undefeated 130-run partnership and seem difficult to get dislodged from the crease. Both of them have matched each other stroke for stroke, although the former skipper has been watchful in his stint so far. The southpaw has been at his attacking best.
Served in line of the stumps, flicked away to square leg. TEA, DAY 1!
Last ball before Tea...

Rahim goes back in the crease and defends it off a straight bat.

250 up for Bangladesh! This full ball is eased down to long on for one. How one sided has this game been so far! The hosts are just cruising along at the moment and the visitors are left wondering as to how they can make inroads into the opposition.

Rahim gets on the front foot and blocks it firmly.
Fuller in length, driven back to the bowler.
Floated in line of the stumps, turned to mid-wicket for nothing.
Floated outside off, eased through covers for one.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Another one outside off, Rahim goes back and guides it past slip for one. It was too close to cut, actually.
Lakshan bowls this from round the wicket, it spins in. Mushfiqur goes back and bunts it down.
Straighter one outside off, punched through covers for one.
On the pads, Rahim flicks it away to short fine leg. Haque calls him over for a quick single and makes it in comfortably.
Outside off, driven straight to sweeper for one.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended towards mid-wicket from the crease.
Served on the stumps, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Rahim keeps this out towards mid-wicket.
Short outside off, cut away through point for one.
Bowled on the stumps, blocked off the front foot.

Eased through covers for one.
